content.title: Myocardial infarction with non-obstructive coronary arteries
content.definition: Myocardial infarction with non-obstructive coronary arteries (MINOCA) refers to the clinical situation when a patient presents with symptoms suggestive of acute coronary syndrome (ACS), demonstrates troponin elevation, and has non-obstructive coronary arteries at the time of coronary angiography (defined as coronary artery stenosis <50% in any major epicardial vessel).
content.prevalence: Reported prevalence of MINOCA varies widely across studies (around 1% to 14% of patients with ACS undergoing angiography).
content.overview_note: MINOCA is an umbrella term that encompasses a heterogeneous group of underlying causes including both coronary and non-coronary pathologies, with the latter including both cardiac and extra-cardiac disorders.

The figure outlines some potential differential diagnoses in patients with a working diagnosis of MINOCA after coronary angiography, but the list is not exhaustive.
